the development of algorithms for software agents that learn to behave in a multi-agent electronic marketplace environment.
the following: (1) how to learn a reputation model for an agent in a market environment, and (2) how to use the model to guide the agent's decision-making.
the development of algorithms that enable personal agents to make informed decisions on whether to trade with a given partner, and on what price to offer.

the proposed algorithms are effective and feasible for the purpose of learning in electronic marketplaces.

the proposed algorithms are able to learn to make decisions that are in the best interest of the agents, even when they are faced with a highly dynamic, uncertain, open, and untrusted market environment.

our algorithms are able to learn to make effective and feasible trading decisions, and that the learning process is robust to changes in the marketplace and to changes in the behaviour of other agents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed and developed a reputation modelling and learning approach for buying agents, and a reinforcement learning approach for selling agents.
we propose a reputation-based RL algorithm for a buyer and a seller agent in an electronic market environment.
we are developing a framework for learning agents in uncertain and untrusted environments, where the agents can use their past experiences to learn the best actions to take in the current situation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of reputation modelling and RL is a very promising research direction.
, in order to achieve a high level of trust and reputation in a marketplace environment, agents must be able to adapt to the changing conditions and the actions of other agents.
the use of RL in the context of reputation modelling in electronic markets provides the basis for a more effective and efficient way of learning the optimal strategies of agents in such environments.
